record.file_problem: Repository text provides metadata, README, and file list only; linked tutorial and results files are not included.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports results from a directional-ablation study on a 3.7B chat model, but does not establish that it uses the original difference-in-means direction or the original all-layer, all-position procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports clear-attempt counts for directional interventions at depths 34 and 28. It lists public aggregate results and annotations in other files, but their contents are not provided, so no additional results are recorded.
record.test_reason: The study applies Arditi et al.'s directional ablation (credited, with harmful_behaviors and harmless_alpaca data) to a new 3.7B chat model, TwIL-LM3-Pro. It reports held-out clear-attempt counts and releases edited float32 and GGUF weights. The direction construction, ablation scope and the 'clear attempt' measure are not specified in the README, so this is T2, not T1.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The README says the most separated activation direction (depth 34) was not the best causal intervention: it gave zero clear attempts in selection. The depth-28 direction gave 22/30 in selection and 50/70 on the reserved float32 condition, and the edited models were released.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a directional-ablation study but does not state that it uses the original difference-in-means direction or all-layer, all-position projection. This is an archival research-materials package and tutorial, not a tested one-command reproduction.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes differ by intervention depth: depth 34 versus depth 28. The README also distinguishes the selection result from the reserved float32 condition.
record.problems: The README does not define clear attempts or provide raw prompts and responses, model weights, or the private blinded packet. It says the complete fresh-machine preparation/extraction pipeline is not supplied and that the code is not a tested one-command reproduction.
record.rows_left_out: No additional README-reported outcomes were left out. The listed RESULTS.md, TUTORIAL.md, and other result files were not provided, so their contents could not be extracted.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the direction; preservation of general capabilities; whether the direction is difference-in-means and ablated at all layers and positions (not stated).
Capability cost of the released edited weights; GGUF-quantized model results (not reported in the README).

missing.what: Refusal or clear-attempt rate of the unmodified base chat model on the same reserved set (baseline)
Any capability or coherence evaluation of the edited model, and GGUF reserved-set results
Definition of 'clear attempt' and the blind-rater agreement figures

record.verdict_notes: Repository README only; the results files are not included. The depth-34 versus depth-28 contrast shows that the most separated layer is not the most causal. The original already selects layers by causal effect, so this is not treated as a challenge to V1. The reader's 'challenges' label on r1 is dropped because r1 is a selection value.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not specify how the direction was constructed, whether it was the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, or whether ablation covered every layer and position. It reports no addition intervention or general-capability measure.
No released-model weight edit or abliteration result is reported in the README.
No jailbreak suppression or training-against-ablation result is reported in the README.
No comparison of one direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is reported in the README.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported in the README.
No cross-language, cross-model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer result is reported in the README.
No comparison of refusal training procedures or training stages is reported in the README.
No reasoning-model result is reported in the README.
